literature.headline_zh: SARS-CoV-2本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 分析显示,尽管病毒持续多样化,Mpro 的 进化 在最普遍的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异株中仍保持显著的限制,其活性位点和二聚化界面区域的氨基酸替换非常有限。 [10.1002/prot.70183]
GSK-3抑制被发现可延迟子代病毒从被感染细胞中释放,且严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体中的NR203M和NR204R 突变减少了GSK-3介导的磷酸化效率。 [10.1111/bph.70679]
联合接种这两种B/HPIV3 媒介扩大了S特异性抗体反应的广度,覆盖了每种媒介单独接种所诱导的反应范围。接种混合疫苗的仓鼠对祖先和近期流行的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株均产生了中和抗体,并在接种后5个月对BA.5/Omicron挑战表现出保护作用。 [10.1128/jvi.00938-26]

在研究 I 中,77% 的 CLL 患者需要住院治疗,24% 需要重症监护,大约 30% 死亡。在研究 II 中,60% 的 CLL 患者出现血清转化,抗体滴度较低,而 29% 的患者观察到 T 细胞反应。在研究 IV 中,94% 的 CLL 患者接受了两剂 疫苗,88% 接受了三剂,78% 接受了四剂,56% 接受了五剂 疫苗。在研究 V 中,与对照组相比,CLL 患者 90 天全因 死亡率 的调整后风险比为 1.70,年轻患者和某些 治疗 患者的风险较高。 [10.69622/33228144]
儿科长新冠的患病率从奥密克戎变种之前的10-25%下降到当前时代的2-8%,这主要受到新冠疫苗接种覆盖率和混合免疫的影响。最持久的临床表现从系统性疲劳、头痛和呼吸困难转变为持续性疲劳、神经认知功能障碍、情绪障碍和自主神经功能障碍。 [10.18203/2349-3291.ijcp20263317]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The analysis showed that despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained, with limited amino-acid substitutions in the active-site and dimerization-interface regions across the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 variants. [10.1002/prot.70183]

GSK-3 inhibition was found to delay the release of progeny virus from infected cells, and the NR203M and NR204R mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants reduced the efficiency of GSK-3-mediated phosphorylation. [10.1111/bph.70679]
Co-administration of the two B/HPIV3 vectors increased the breadth of the S-specific antibody response, spanning the breadth elicited by each vector individually. [10.1128/jvi.00938-26]

In Study I, 77% of CLL patients required hospitalization, 24% needed intensive care, and approximately 30% died. In Study II, 60% of CLL patients seroconverted with low antibody titers, while T cell responses were observed in 29% of patients. [10.69622/33228144]

The prevalence of pediatric Long COVID decreased from 10–25% during the pre-Omicron variants to 2–8% in the post-Omicron era, largely influenced by vaccination coverage and hybrid immunity. [10.18203/2349-3291.ijcp20263317]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.

papers.title: Incidence and Outcomes of Bloodstream Infections in Critically Ill Patients with COVID-19: A Nationwide Multicenter Study in South Korea.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) increases the risk of bloodstream infections (BSI), but associated risk factors remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to evaluate BSI risk factors in patients admitted to the intensive care unit for COVID-19. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This nationwide multicenter study, conducted across 22 university-affiliated hospitals in South Korea, included COVID-19 patients treated with high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy or mechanical ventilation. Baseline characteristics were compared between patients who developed BSI within 30 days and those who did not. Pathogens were analyzed, risk factors were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, and supplementary Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed to address time-dependent outcomes. RESULTS: Of 573 included patients, 206 (35.9%) developed at least one BSI episode. Staphylococcus species were the most frequent isolates. Gram-negative bacteria became increasingly prevalent over time, while fungal infections were associated with prolonged hospitalization. Multivariable analysis identified chronic neurological disease, higher baseline Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, mechanical ventilation, prone positioning, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) use prior to infection as independent BSI predictors. Notably, although crude in-hospital mortality was significantly higher in the BSI group (41.5% vs. 31.7%, p=0.012), BSI was not an independent predictor of in-hospital mortality in either logistic regression or Cox analyses. CONCLUSION: In critically ill patients with COVID-19, high baseline severity, chronic neurological disease, and pre-infection advanced life support (mechanical ventilation and ECMO) were independent predictors of BSI. Rather than acting as an independent cause of death, BSI primarily serves as a clinical marker of extreme illness severity and prolonged invasive interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the risk factors for bloodstream infections (BSI) in critically ill patients with COVID-19 admitted to intensive care units in South Korea. A nationwide multicenter study across 22 hospitals included patients treated with high-flow nasal cannula or mechanical ventilation. Pathogens were analyzed, and risk factors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards analyses. Of 573 patients, 35.9% developed at least one BSI episode, with Staphylococcus species being the most common. Gram-negative bacteria increased in prevalence over time, and fungal infections were linked to prolonged hospitalization. Independent predictors of BSI included chronic neurological disease, higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores, and prior use of mechanical ventilation or ECMO. Despite higher crude mortality in the BSI group, BSI was not an independent predictor of mortality. The findings highlight BSI as a marker of severe illness and prolonged interventions rather than a direct cause of death. The study provides insights into BSI risk factors in critically ill COVID-19 patients, which could inform clinical management and surveillance strategies.

papers.title: Evolution of the SARS ‐ CoV ‐2 Main Protease Under Fitness Constraints Imposed by Folding Stability and Activity
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) continues to evolve and diversify, leading to the emergence of immune‐evasive variants and underscoring the need for complementary antiviral strategies targeting conserved viral machinery. In this context, the main protease (Mpro) represents a potential therapeutic target because of its central role in viral replication and its low similarity to human proteases. However, the evolutionary consequences of Mpro variation on substrate recognition and potential resistance remain insufficiently explored. Through the analysis of multiple SARS‐CoV‐2 Mpro variants, we show that, despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained since the emergence of the Omicron‐associated P132H lineage in 2022, with limited amino‐acid substitutions in the active‐site and dimerization‐interface regions. Across the most prevalent SARS‐CoV‐2 variants, overall substrate recognition by Mpro was largely preserved, although specific variant‐substrate pairs exhibited some heterogeneity in per‐residue interactions and hydrogen‐bond patterns. Ensemble dynamics revealed conserved large‐scale motions alongside modest substrate‐dependent shifts in secondary motions in certain Mpro variants. Overall, SARS‐CoV‐2 Mpro evolution is strongly constrained by structural and functional requirements, supporting the suitability of this protein as an effective antiviral target. The findings further suggest that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics may help inform the design of therapeutic strategies with improved long‐term robustness.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the evolutionary constraints on the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) due to its structural and functional requirements, highlighting the need for complementary antiviral strategies targeting conserved viral machinery.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants, focusing on their evolution since the emergence of the Omicron-associated P132H lineage in 2022, and examined their structural and functional characteristics across prevalent variants.
analysis.methods: The researchers conducted an analysis of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants using ensemble dynamics to assess large-scale motions and substrate-dependent shifts in secondary motions, while also evaluating substrate recognition and interactions across variants.
analysis.main_results: The analysis showed that despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained, with limited amino-acid substitutions in the active-site and dimerization-interface regions across the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that Mpro evolution is strongly constrained by structural and functional requirements, which supports its use as an effective antiviral target, and suggest that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics could improve the robustness of therapeutic strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the design of more robust therapeutic strategies against SARS-CoV-2 by considering its evolutionary dynamics, which could enhance long-term antiviral efficacy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on analysis of multiple variants, but the evidence is limited to structural and functional observations, with no direct clinical or epidemiological outcomes reported.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the evolutionary constraints on the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) due to its structural and functional requirements. The researchers analyzed multiple Mpro variants, showing that despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained since the emergence of the Omicron-associated P132H lineage in 2022, with limited amino-acid substitutions in key regions. papers.title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 主蛋白酶在折叠稳定性与活性约束下的进化限制
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT The severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) continues to evolve and diversify, leading to the emergence of immune‐evasive variants and underscoring the need for complementary antiviral strategies targeting conserved viral machinery. In this context, the main protease (Mpro) represents a potential therapeutic target because of its central role in viral replication and its low similarity to human proteases. However, the evolutionary consequences of Mpro variation on substrate recognition and potential resistance remain insufficiently explored. Through the analysis of multiple SARS‐CoV‐2 Mpro variants, we show that, despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained since the emergence of the Omicron‐associated P132H lineage in 2022, with limited amino‐acid substitutions in the active‐site and dimerization‐interface regions. Across the most prevalent SARS‐CoV‐2 variants, overall substrate recognition by Mpro was largely preserved, although specific variant‐substrate pairs exhibited some heterogeneity in per‐residue interactions and hydrogen‐bond patterns. Ensemble dynamics revealed conserved large‐scale motions alongside modest substrate‐dependent shifts in secondary motions in certain Mpro variants. Overall, SARS‐CoV‐2 Mpro evolution is strongly constrained by structural and functional requirements, supporting the suitability of this protein as an effective antiviral target. The findings further suggest that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics may help inform the design of therapeutic strategies with improved long‐term robustness.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)持续进化和多样化,导致免疫逃逸变异株的出现,凸显了需要针对保守病毒机制的互补性 抗病毒药物 策略的重要性。在此背景下,主蛋白酶(Mpro)因其在病毒复制中的核心作用以及与人类蛋白酶低相似性,代表了一个潜在的治疗靶点。然而,Mpro 变异对底物识别和潜在抗性的影响仍缺乏充分研究。通过对多种 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变异株的分析,我们发现,尽管病毒持续多样化,自2022年与奥密克戎相关的P132H谱系出现以来,Mpro 的 进化 保持了显著的限制,其活性位点和二聚化界面区域的氨基酸替换非常有限。在最普遍的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异株中,Mpro 对底物的整体识别基本保持不变,尽管某些变异株与底物的配对在每个残基的相互作用和氢键模式上表现出一定的异质性。集合动力学分析揭示了某些 Mpro 变异株中保守的大尺度运动,以及在某些情况下与底物相关的次要运动的适度变化。总体而言,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 主蛋白酶的 进化 强烈受到结构和功能需求的限制,支持其作为有效 抗病毒药物 靶点的适用性。研究结果进一步表明,考虑病毒的进化动态可能有助于设计更具长期稳健性的治疗策略。

papers.title: Repositioning niclosamide and alectinib to inhibit the hyperphosphorylation of SARS‐CoV‐2's nucleocapsid protein
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: In the past two decades, three pathogenic coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, spilled over from natural animal reservoirs into the human population. Upon entry into infected cells, the nucleocapsid (N) protein of coronavirus becomes heavily phosphorylated within its central Ser-Arg domain by host kinase GSK-3, which triggers genomic RNA unpackaging and facilitates its recruitment to the replication transcription complex. Although initially considered a promising antiviral strategy, inhibiting N hyperphosphorylation requires high concentrations of kinase inhibitor and is impractical to achieve by conventional pharmacological means. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: We investigated the effect of GSK-3 inhibition on SARS-CoV-2 replication in Calu-3 and Vero E6 cells. The dose-dependent effect of the GSK-3 inhibitor to block N hyperphosphorylation was examined in 293T cells heterologously expressing the viral protein. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analysis was performed to evaluate the phosphorylation profile of the purified N protein. KEY RESULTS: GSK-3 inhibition delays the release of progeny virus from infected cells. N hyperphosphorylation relies on a complex, redundant priming mechanism and exhibits strong cooperativity, which together contribute to resistance against GSK-3 inhibitors. The NR203M and NR203K/G204R mutations-present in the delta and omicron variants of concern (VOCs), respectively-reduce the efficiency of GSK-3-mediated phosphorylation. We discovered a novel pharmacological tool combining niclosamide and alectinib that partially degrades GSK-3 and restores the sensitivity of N hyperphosphorylation to the clinically tested GSK-3 inhibitor, enzastaurin. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: This work provides the biochemical basis for a novel approach to treat COVID-19 by synergistically repositioning two FDA-approved drugs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of inhibiting SARS-CoV-2's nucleocapsid protein hyperphosphorylation, a process critical for viral replication and genomic RNA unpackaging.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Calu-3 and Vero E6 cells to investigate the effect of GSK-3 inhibition on SARS-CoV-2 replication, with a focus on the virus's nucleocapsid protein and its phosphorylation dynamics.
analysis.methods: The researchers used liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry to evaluate the phosphorylation profile of the purified N protein and examined the dose-dependent effect of GSK-3 inhibitors in 293T cells expressing the viral protein.
analysis.main_results: GSK-3 inhibition was found to delay the release of progeny virus from infected cells, and the NR203M and NR204R mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants reduced the efficiency of GSK-3-mediated phosphorylation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as evidence for a novel pharmacological approach that combines niclosamide and alectinib to partially degrade GSK-3 and restore sensitivity to the clinically tested inhibitor enzastaurin.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a potential new strategy for treating COVID-19 by targeting the phosphorylation of SARS-CoV-2's nucleocapsid protein through the repositioning of existing drugs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited to in vitro experiments, and the observed effects on viral release may not fully translate to in vivo settings, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of repositioning niclosamide and alectinib to inhibit the hyperphosphorylation of SARS-CoV-2's nucleocapsid protein, a process mediated by host kinase GSK-3. The research highlights the challenges of conventional kinase inhibition due to the complex and redundant priming mechanism of N hyperphosphorylation. The authors demonstrate that GSK-3 inhibition delays progeny virus release in infected cells and that mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants reduce the efficiency of this process. They propose a novel pharmacological strategy combining niclosamide and alectinib to partially degrade GSK-3 and restore sensitivity to clinically tested inhibitors. While the findings offer a biochemical basis for a new treatment approach, the study's reliance on in vitro models limits its direct applicability to clinical settings, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: In the past two decades, three pathogenic coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, spilled over from natural animal reservoirs into the human population. Upon entry into infected cells, the nucleocapsid (N) protein of coronavirus becomes heavily phosphorylated within its central Ser-Arg domain by host kinase GSK-3, which triggers genomic RNA unpackaging and facilitates its recruitment to the replication transcription complex. Although initially considered a promising antiviral strategy, inhibiting N hyperphosphorylation requires high concentrations of kinase inhibitor and is impractical to achieve by conventional pharmacological means. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: We investigated the effect of GSK-3 inhibition on SARS-CoV-2 replication in Calu-3 and Vero E6 cells. The dose-dependent effect of the GSK-3 inhibitor to block N hyperphosphorylation was examined in 293T cells heterologously expressing the viral protein. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analysis was performed to evaluate the phosphorylation profile of the purified N protein. KEY RESULTS: GSK-3 inhibition delays the release of progeny virus from infected cells. N hyperphosphorylation relies on a complex, redundant priming mechanism and exhibits strong cooperativity, which together contribute to resistance against GSK-3 inhibitors. The NR203M and NR203K/G204R mutations-present in the delta and omicron variants of concern (VOCs), respectively-reduce the efficiency of GSK-3-mediated phosphorylation. We discovered a novel pharmacological tool combining niclosamide and alectinib that partially degrades GSK-3 and restores the sensitivity of N hyperphosphorylation to the clinically tested GSK-3 inhibitor, enzastaurin. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: This work provides the biochemical basis for a novel approach to treat COVID-19 by synergistically repositioning two FDA-approved drugs.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决抑制严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的核衣壳蛋白过度磷酸化的问题,这一过程对病毒复制和基因组RNA解包至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在Calu-3和Vero E6细胞中进行,以探讨GSK-3抑制对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2复制的影响,重点关注病毒的核衣壳蛋白及其磷酸化动态。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用液相色谱-串联质谱技术评估了纯化N蛋白的磷酸化谱型,并在表达病毒蛋白的293T细胞中检查了GSK-3抑制剂的剂量依赖效应。
analysis_zh.main_results: GSK-3抑制被发现可延迟子代病毒从被感染细胞中释放,且严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体中的NR203M和NR204R 突变减少了GSK-3介导的磷酸化效率。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为一种新型药理学方法的证据,该方法结合尼氯胺和阿来替尼部分降解GSK-3并恢复对已临床测试的抑制剂恩扎斯塔林的敏感性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据仅限于体外实验,观察到的对病毒释放的影响可能无法完全适用于体内环境,因此得出中等置信度的评估。

papers.title: Long COVID in the pediatric population – clinical evolution, prevalence and management from the early pandemic to the current era: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), or Long COVID, in the pediatric population present a complex clinical picture that has evolved from the initial pandemic waves to the current era characterized by omicron lineages and widespread vaccination. Understanding its prevalence, clinical trajectory, and evidence-based therapeutic strategies remains crucial for pediatric healthcare. Objective of the study was to systematically evaluate the clinical evolution, changing prevalence rates, predominant symptom clusters, and therapeutic management strategies of Long COVID in pediatric patients from the early pandemic to the current era. Systematic review of literature published between 2020 and 2026 across PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and Embase. Observational studies, prospective cohort analyses, and clinical trial data assessing post-acute symptoms (≥12 weeks post-infection) in children and adolescents aged 0–18 years were included following PRISMA guidelines. Reported prevalence of pediatric Long COVID varied significantly across pandemic phases, decreasing from 10–25% during pre-Omicron variants to 2–8% in the post-Omicron era, largely moderated by pediatric vaccination coverage and previous hybrid immunity. The most persistent clinical manifestations shifted from systemic fatigue, headache, and dyspnea to persistent fatigue, neurocognitive dysfunction ("brain fog"), mood disturbances, and dysautonomia (e.g., POTS-like symptoms). Management strategies remain primarily multidisciplinary and symptom-targeted, focusing on tailored physical rehabilitation, cognitive pacing, and non-pharmacological interventions, with emerging evidence supporting pharmacological targeting of post-viral inflammatory and autonomic dysregulation. Long COVID in pediatric populations continues to present a dynamic clinical burden, with reduced overall incidence in recent years but persistent morbidity in vulnerable subsets. Integrated, multidisciplinary follow-up models and standardized diagnostic criteria are essential to optimize long-term clinical management and functional recovery in pediatric patients.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the clinical evolution, prevalence, and management of Long COVID in pediatric populations from the early pandemic to the current era. It highlights the significant decrease in prevalence, influenced by vaccination and hybrid immunity, and the shift in persistent symptoms from systemic manifestations to neurocognitive and autonomic issues. The study underscores the importance of multidisciplinary approaches and standardized diagnostic criteria for effective management. While the review is based on observational data and presents variability in findings, the comprehensive methodology and inclusion of diverse sources support its conclusions. The results have important implications for understanding and addressing the long-term health impacts of SARS-CoV-2 in children.

papers.abstract_zh: 新型冠状病毒感染后急性后遗症(PASC),即长新冠,在儿科人群中呈现出复杂的临床图景,其演变从最初的疫情浪潮发展到以奥密克戎变种为主导、广泛传播的当前时代。理解其演变、临床轨迹及基于证据的治疗策略对于儿科医疗保健至关重要。本研究的目的是系统评估从早期大流行到当前时代,儿科患者长新冠的临床表现、演变率变化、主要症状群及管理策略。系统综述了2020年至2026年间在PubMed、Scopus、Cochrane Library和Embase上发表的文献。根据PRISMA指南,纳入了观察性研究、前瞻性队列分析以及评估儿童和青少年(0-18岁)感染后12周及以上急性后症状的临床试验数据。报告的儿科长新冠患病率在疫情各阶段显著变化,从奥密克戎变种之前的10-25%下降到当前时代的2-8%,这主要受到儿科新冠疫苗接种覆盖率和先前混合免疫的影响。最持久的临床表现从系统性疲劳、头痛和呼吸困难转变为持续性疲劳、神经认知功能障碍("脑雾")、情绪障碍和自主神经功能障碍(如POTS样症状)。管理策略仍主要以多学科和症状针对性为主,侧重于定制化的身体康复、认知节律调节和非药物干预,有新兴证据支持针对病毒后炎症和自主神经失调的药物治疗。长新冠在儿科人群中持续呈现动态的临床负担,近年来总体患病率有所下降,但在易感亚群中仍存在持续的发病率。整合的多学科随访模式和标准化的诊断标准对于优化儿科长新冠患者的长期临床管理和功能恢复至关重要。

papers.title: Childhood and adolescent immunisation intentions post-COVID-19 in Lusaka, Zambia
papers.abstract: Background: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, parental delays and refusals of well-established, safe, and effective childhood vaccinations have contributed to the resurgence of infectious diseases. This raises concerns that COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy may also extend to novel vaccines for children when introduced in the future. This study examined caregivers’, who included healthcare workers (HCWs), perceptions of novel vaccinations for children ages 0-17 years old and intentions to vaccinate children and adolescents ages 12-17 years against COVID-19. Methods: We conducted a secondary data analysis of a larger cross-sectional survey administered to parents/caregivers of children ages 0-17 years in Lusaka, Zambia, between 13 November and 15 December 2023. Vaccination intention for COVID-19 was specifically focused on caregivers of adolescents ages 12-17 years, following COVID-19 vaccination guidelines during the study. Descriptive statistics were used to explore demographic characteristics, vaccination history, and caregivers’ COVID-19 vaccination status, along with their children’s routine childhood vaccine histories and perceptions of COVID-19 and novel vaccinations. Results: Among 277 caregivers (66.8% women, median age: 35 years), 93.1% reported that their child had received all recommended routine childhood vaccinations. COVID-19 vaccine uptake was higher among HCWs (68.2% with ≥2 doses) than among community members (40.8%) and having ≥2 doses was associated with higher COVID-19 vaccine uptake among their adolescents ages 12-17 years. 58.0% of caregivers indicated that their 12-17 years old adolescents had received at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose. Overall intention to further vaccinate children against COVID-19, especially among those already unvaccinated, remained low, with 24.7% of caregivers reporting no intent to vaccinate their children. Protection from hospitalization and death from malaria, TB, HIV, pneumonia, influenza, and diarrheal diseases were the most cited reason (79.1%) for intention to vaccinate children with novel vaccines for these diseases. The most prominent reasons for reluctance towards future vaccines were the fear of potential side effects (45.5%) and insufficient knowledge about vaccination benefits and risks (31.8%). Caregivers most trusted the Ministry of Health (86.6%) and healthcare professionals (66.8%) as sources of vaccine information. Conclusions: While routine childhood vaccine uptake remained high, acceptance of COVID-19 and future novel vaccines for children was lower and was influenced by caregivers’ own vaccination status. Targeted and transparent communication through trusted sources such as the Ministry of Health and healthcare professionals may be critical for addressing safety concerns and strengthening confidence in novel childhood vaccines.

papers.title_zh: Childhood and adolescent immunisation intentions post-COVID-19 in Lusaka, Zambia
papers.source_body_en: Background: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, parental delays and refusals of well-established, safe, and effective childhood vaccinations have contributed to the resurgence of infectious diseases. This raises concerns that COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy may also extend to novel vaccines for children when introduced in the future. This study examined caregivers’, who included healthcare workers (HCWs), perceptions of novel vaccinations for children ages 0-17 years old and intentions to vaccinate children and adolescents ages 12-17 years against COVID-19. Methods: We conducted a secondary data analysis of a larger cross-sectional survey administered to parents/caregivers of children ages 0-17 years in Lusaka, Zambia, between 13 November and 15 December 2023. Vaccination intention for COVID-19 was specifically focused on caregivers of adolescents ages 12-17 years, following COVID-19 vaccination guidelines during the study. Descriptive statistics were used to explore demographic characteristics, vaccination history, and caregivers’ COVID-19 vaccination status, along with their children’s routine childhood vaccine histories and perceptions of COVID-19 and novel vaccinations. Results: Among 277 caregivers (66.8% women, median age: 35 years), 93.1% reported that their child had received all recommended routine childhood vaccinations. COVID-19 vaccine uptake was higher among HCWs (68.2% with ≥2 doses) than among community members (40.8%) and having ≥2 doses was associated with higher COVID-19 vaccine uptake among their adolescents ages 12-17 years. 58.0% of caregivers indicated that their 12-17 years old adolescents had received at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose. Overall intention to further vaccinate children against COVID-19, especially among those already unvaccinated, remained low, with 24.7% of caregivers reporting no intent to vaccinate their children. Protection from hospitalization and death from malaria, TB, HIV, pneumonia, influenza, and diarrheal diseases were the most cited reason (79.1%) for intention to vaccinate children with novel vaccines for these diseases. The most prominent reasons for reluctance towards future vaccines were the fear of potential side effects (45.5%) and insufficient knowledge about vaccination benefits and risks (31.8%). Caregivers most trusted the Ministry of Health (86.6%) and healthcare professionals (66.8%) as sources of vaccine information. Conclusions: While routine childhood vaccine uptake remained high, acceptance of COVID-19 and future novel vaccines for children was lower and was influenced by caregivers’ own vaccination status. Targeted and transparent communication through trusted sources such as the Ministry of Health and healthcare professionals may be critical for addressing safety concerns and strengthening confidence in novel childhood vaccines.

papers.title: Co-administration of intranasal parainfluenza virus vaccines expressing antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 S antigens elicits broad and durable immunity in hamsters
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Intranasal COVID-19 vaccines with the ability to induce broad and durable mucosal and systemic immunity would be useful as stand-alone vaccines or in combination with injectable vaccines. We evaluated in hamsters the breadth of immunity and durability of protection elicited by co-administration of two live-attenuated bovine/human parainfluenza virus type 3 (B/HPIV3) vectors expressing antigenically distinct prefusion-stabilized S proteins of the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 isolate (B/HPIV3/S-6P) or the BA.5/Omicron variant (B/HPIV3/S-BA.5-2P). These vectors are being developed as bivalent pediatric vaccines against HPIV3 and SARS-CoV-2 and are based on bovine PIV3 with the fusion (F) and hemagglutinin-neuraminidase (HN) glycoproteins replaced by those of human PIV3. To broaden the S-specific antibody response, we evaluated co-administration of these B/HPIV3 S-expressing vectors. Each B/HPIV3 S-expressing vector induced robust serum anti-S IgG and IgA antibody levels to the antigen-matched S protein that were sustained for at least 5 months. Co-administration increased the breadth of the S-specific antibody response, spanning the breadth of the response elicited by each vector individually. Hamsters immunized intranasally with the mixture of vectors developed neutralizing antibodies to ancestral and recently circulating SARS-CoV-2 strains and were protected against BA.5/Omicron challenge 5 months after immunization, with no weight loss, SARS-CoV-2 challenge virus replication, or increase in host inflammatory cytokines in the airways after the challenge, indicating durable protection. Thus, intranasal co-administration of live-attenuated B/HPIV3 expressing antigenically distinct S proteins induced broad and durable antibody responses, and long-term protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge. This approach warrants further development and may better protect against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants. IMPORTANCE Intranasal SARS-CoV-2 vaccines that induce systemic and local mucosal immunity hold promise, especially as booster vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 variants. We developed live-attenuated bovine/human parainfluenza virus type 3 (B/HPIV3)-vectored vaccines as bivalent pediatric vaccines against PIV3 and SARS-CoV-2. Co-administration in a single dose of two B/HPIV3 vectors, one expressing the spike protein S from the ancestral Wuhan-Hu-1 strain and one expressing S of BA.5/Omicron, induced broad serum anti-S antibody responses that remained strong for at least 5 months. Hamsters challenged with the BA.5/Omicron strain 5 months after immunization were protected from weight loss, inflammatory responses, and challenge virus replication in the airways. Thus, in the hamster model, intranasal co-administration of live-attenuated B/HPIV3 expressing SARS-CoV-2 S elicits protection durable over several months, and combining two antigenically distinct B/HPIV3 S-expressing vectors substantially broadens the antibody response. This mucosal immunization approach may provide durable and broad protection against SARS-CoV-2.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in hamsters using two B/HPIV3 vectors expressing the spike protein from the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 isolate (B/HPIV3/S-6P) and the BA.5/Omicron variant (B/HPIV3/S-BA.5-2P). The design involved co-administration of these vectors to assess immune responses and protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge.
analysis.methods: The researchers developed live-attenuated B/HPIV3 vectors with human PIV3 glycoproteins and evaluated their ability to induce anti-S IgG and IgA antibody levels in hamsters. They also assessed neutralizing antibody responses and protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that co-administration of B/HPIV3 vectors expressing antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins can elicit broad and durable immunity, which may offer better protection against emerging variants.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that this mucosal immunization approach could provide durable and broad protection against SARS-CoV-2, potentially improving vaccine strategies for combating emerging variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a hamster model, which may not fully represent human immune responses. However, the evidence is strong as it demonstrates durable protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge with no weight loss or inflammatory responses observed.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immune response and protection elicited by co-administering two live-attenuated bovine/human parainfluenza virus type 3 (B/HPIV3) vectors expressing antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins in hamsters. The vectors were designed to induce broad and durable mucosal and systemic immunity. The authors suggest that this approach may offer improved protection against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants. The study is limited to a hamster model, but the evidence supports the durability and breadth of immunity induced by the vaccine strategy.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估在仓鼠中,联合接种两种表达抗原不同的活化牛/人副流感病毒3型(B/HPIV3)媒介(分别表达祖先严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2分离株和BA.5/Omicron变种的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白)所诱导的免疫广度和保护持久性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在仓鼠中进行,使用两种表达来自祖先严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2分离株(B/HPIV3/S-6P)和BA.5/Omicron变种(B/HPIV3/S-BA.5-2P)的刺突蛋白的B/HPIV3 媒介。研究设计包括联合接种这些媒介以评估免疫广度和对BA.5/Omicron挑战的保护效果。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员开发了携带人类PIV3糖蛋白的活化B/HPIV3 媒介,并评估了其在仓鼠中诱导抗S IgG和IgA抗体水平的能力。他们还评估了中和抗体反应和对BA.5/Omicron挑战的保护效果。
elements_zh.main_results: 联合接种这两种B/HPIV3 媒介扩大了S特异性抗体反应的广度,覆盖了每种媒介单独接种所诱导的反应范围。接种混合疫苗的仓鼠对祖先和近期流行的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株均产生了中和抗体,并在接种后5个月对BA.5/Omicron挑战表现出保护作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明联合接种表达抗原不同的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白的B/HPIV3 媒介可诱导广泛且持久的免疫,这可能为对抗新兴变种提供更好的保护。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,这种黏膜免疫方法可能为严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2提供持久且广泛的保护,从而可能改善针对新兴变种的疫苗策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于仓鼠模型,可能无法完全代表人类的免疫应答。然而,证据较强,因为它展示了对BA.5/Omicron挑战的持久保护,且未观察到体重减轻或炎症反应。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the breadth of immunity and durability of protection elicited by co-administration of two live-attenuated bovine/human parainfluenza virus type 3 (B/HPIV3) vectors expressing antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins in hamsters.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in hamsters using two B/HPIV3 vectors expressing the spike protein from the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 isolate (B/HPIV3/S-6P) and the BA.5/Omicron variant (B/HPIV3/S-BA.5-2P). The design involved co-administration of these vectors to assess immune responses and protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers developed live-attenuated B/HPIV3 vectors with human PIV3 glycoproteins and evaluated their ability to induce anti-S IgG and IgA antibody levels in hamsters. They also assessed neutralizing antibody responses and protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge.
analysis_en.main_results: Co-administration of the two B/HPIV3 vectors increased the breadth of the S-specific antibody response, spanning the breadth elicited by each vector individually. Hamsters immunized with the mixture developed neutralizing antibodies to both ancestral and recently circulating SARS-CoV-2 strains and were protected against BA.5/Omicron challenge 5 months post-immunization.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that co-administration of B/HPIV3 vectors expressing antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins can elicit broad and durable immunity, which may offer better protection against emerging variants.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that this mucosal immunization approach could provide durable and broad protection against SARS-CoV-2, potentially improving vaccine strategies for combating emerging variants.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a hamster model, which may not fully represent human immune responses. However, the evidence is strong as it demonstrates durable protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge with no weight loss or inflammatory responses observed.

papers.title_zh: 鼻内联合接种表达抗原不同的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 S抗原的活疫苗疫苗可在仓鼠中诱导广泛且持久的免疫
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Intranasal COVID-19 vaccines with the ability to induce broad and durable mucosal and systemic immunity would be useful as stand-alone vaccines or in combination with injectable vaccines. We evaluated in hamsters the breadth of immunity and durability of protection elicited by co-administration of two live-attenuated bovine/human parainfluenza virus type 3 (B/HPIV3) vectors expressing antigenically distinct prefusion-stabilized S proteins of the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 isolate (B/HPIV3/S-6P) or the BA.5/Omicron variant (B/HPIV3/S-BA.5-2P). These vectors are being developed as bivalent pediatric vaccines against HPIV3 and SARS-CoV-2 and are based on bovine PIV3 with the fusion (F) and hemagglutinin-neuraminidase (HN) glycoproteins replaced by those of human PIV3. To broaden the S-specific antibody response, we evaluated co-administration of these B/HPIV3 S-expressing vectors. Each B/HPIV3 S-expressing vector induced robust serum anti-S IgG and IgA antibody levels to the antigen-matched S protein that were sustained for at least 5 months. Co-administration increased the breadth of the S-specific antibody response, spanning the breadth of the response elicited by each vector individually. Hamsters immunized intranasally with the mixture of vectors developed neutralizing antibodies to ancestral and recently circulating SARS-CoV-2 strains and were protected against BA.5/Omicron challenge 5 months after immunization, with no weight loss, SARS-CoV-2 challenge virus replication, or increase in host inflammatory cytokines in the airways after the challenge, indicating durable protection. Thus, intranasal co-administration of live-attenuated B/HPIV3 expressing antigenically distinct S proteins induced broad and durable antibody responses, and long-term protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge. This approach warrants further development and may better protect against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants. IMPORTANCE Intranasal SARS-CoV-2 vaccines that induce systemic and local mucosal immunity hold promise, especially as booster vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 variants. We developed live-attenuated bovine/human parainfluenza virus type 3 (B/HPIV3)-vectored vaccines as bivalent pediatric vaccines against PIV3 and SARS-CoV-2. Co-administration in a single dose of two B/HPIV3 vectors, one expressing the spike protein S from the ancestral Wuhan-Hu-1 strain and one expressing S of BA.5/Omicron, induced broad serum anti-S antibody responses that remained strong for at least 5 months. Hamsters challenged with the BA.5/Omicron strain 5 months after immunization were protected from weight loss, inflammatory responses, and challenge virus replication in the airways. Thus, in the hamster model, intranasal co-administration of live-attenuated B/HPIV3 expressing SARS-CoV-2 S elicits protection durable over several months, and combining two antigenically distinct B/HPIV3 S-expressing vectors substantially broadens the antibody response. This mucosal immunization approach may provide durable and broad protection against SARS-CoV-2.

papers.title: Comparative Burden of COVID-19 in Adults with Rheumatic Diseases and Immunocompetent Individuals: A Population-Based Cohort Study in Quebec, Canada, 2020-2023
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Across major phases of the COVID-19 pandemic (March 2020-April 2023), we compared the burden of severe COVID-19 among individuals with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs) versus immunocompetent individuals with and without comorbidities. Methods This population-based cohort study used administrative datasets to estimate crude and age-and sex-standardized SARS-CoV-2 and severe COVID-19 incidences among adults > 18 years with SARDs, chronic comorbidities, or no comorbidities. Relative to the latter, we used Cox models to derive adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for infection, hospitalization, and intensive care unit admission or death (ICU/death) during the pre-vaccination (March–December 2020), vaccination pre-Omicron (December 2020– December 2021), and Omicron (December 2021–April 2023) periods. Results We included 81,434 adults with SARDs, and 2,020,356 with comorbidities versus 3,144,700 without comorbidities. Despite similar adjusted infection rates, the SARDS cohort had higher risks of hospitalization and ICU/death during the pre-vaccination period (aHRs: 3.4, 95%CI:2.8–4.1; and 4.0, 95%CI:2.8–5.7, respectively), persisting through the Omicron period (aHRs: 4.5, 95%CI:4.0–4.9; and 4.4, 95%CI:3.6–5.4, respectively). Among SARDS, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus contributed highest burden, with comparable hospitalization and mortality rates among younger rheumatoid arthritis versus healthy older adults. Highly immunosuppressive rituximab-or mycophenolate-treated patients had highest hospitalization and ICU/death risks, particularly during the Omicron period (aHRs: 11.9, 95%CI:9.9–14.3; and 17.6, 95%CI:13.0– 23.9, respectively). Conclusion Individuals with SARDs, especially receiving highly immunosuppressive therapies, experienced elevated COVID-19 burden and severe outcome risks throughout the pandemic, warranting their prioritized consideration during future public health emergencies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the burden of severe COVID-19 between individuals with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs) and immunocompetent individuals, addressing the knowledge gap about the impact of rheumatic diseases on pandemic outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This population-based cohort study analyzed administrative datasets from Quebec, Canada, spanning 2020 to 2023, including 81,434 adults with SARDs, 2,020,356 with comorbidities, and 3,144,700 without comorbidities.
analysis.methods: The study used administrative datasets to estimate crude and age- and sex-standardized incidences of SARS-CoV-2 and severe COVID-19, applying Cox models to derive adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for infection, hospitalization, and ICU/death across different pandemic periods.
analysis.main_results: The SARDS cohort had higher risks of hospitalization and ICU/death compared to immunocompetent individuals during the pre-vaccination period (aHRs: 3.4, 95%CI:2.8–4.1; and 4.0, 95%CI:2.8–5.7, respectively), with these risks persisting through the Omicron period (aHRs: 4.5, 95%CI:4.0–4.9; and 4.4, 95%CI:3.6–5.4, respectively).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that individuals with SARDs, particularly those on highly immunosuppressive therapies, faced elevated risks of severe outcomes, highlighting the need for targeted public health strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the prioritization of SARDS patients in public health measures, emphasizing the importance of tailored surveillance and interventions during future pandemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on administrative data, which may introduce biases, and the evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the design and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared the burden of severe COVID-19 among adults with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs) and immunocompetent individuals in Quebec, Canada, from 2020 to 2023. It found that individuals with SARDs had higher risks of hospitalization and ICU/death, particularly during the pre-vaccination and Omicron periods, even after adjusting for age and sex. The results suggest that SARDS patients, especially those on immunosuppressive therapies, require prioritized public health considerations. The study used administrative datasets and Cox models to analyze outcomes, but its observational design and reliance on existing data limit the strength of the evidence, which is assessed as moderate.

Relative to the latter, we used Cox models to derive adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for infection, hospitalization, and intensive care unit admission or death (ICU/death) during the pre-vaccination (March–December 2020), vaccination pre-Omicron (December 2020– December 2021), and Omicron (December 2021–April 2023) periods. Results We included 81,434 adults with SARDs, and 2,020,356 with comorbidities versus 3,144,700 without comorbidities. Despite similar adjusted infection rates, the SARDS cohort had higher risks of hospitalization and ICU/death during the pre-vaccination period (aHRs: 3.4, 95%CI:2.8–4.1; and 4.0, 95%CI:2.8–5.7, respectively), persisting through the Omicron period (aHRs: 4.5, 95%CI:4.0–4.9; and 4.4, 95%CI:3.6–5.4, respectively). Among SARDS, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus contributed highest burden, with comparable hospitalization and mortality rates among younger rheumatoid arthritis versus healthy older adults. Highly immunosuppressive rituximab-or mycophenolate-treated patients had highest hospitalization and ICU/death risks, particularly during the Omicron period (aHRs: 11.9, 95%CI:9.9–14.3; and 17.6, 95%CI:13.0– 23.9, respectively). Conclusion Individuals with SARDs, especially receiving highly immunosuppressive therapies, experienced elevated COVID-19 burden and severe outcome risks throughout the pandemic, warranting their prioritized consideration during future public health emergencies.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Variant-Specific G-Quadruplex Ligands Targeting the Conserved Main Protease of SARS-CoV-2
papers.abstract: Abstract The ongoing SARS-CoV-2 pandemic highlights the need for antivirals effective across emerging variants. Targeting the conserved main protease (Mpro), a key enzyme in viral replication, this study explored G-quadruplex (G4) ligands as variant-specific inhibitors. Analysis of 5.8 million GISAID sequences revealed frequent but catalytically distal mutations K90R (Alpha), G15S (Lambda), and P132H (Omicron, JN.1) guiding the selection of representative Mpro structures for in silico screening. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/GBSA calculations identified four ligands G4L3501 (–36.63 kcal/mol), G4L3503 (–40.39 kcal/mol), G4L3505 (–40.54 kcal/mol), and G4L3506 (–20.32 kcal/mol) that stably occupied the catalytic pocket through conserved interactions with His41, Cys145, Glu166, and Gln189. Per-residue energy decomposition confirmed strong stabilization by active-site residues, consistent with the nirmatrelvir (PF-07321332) binding mode. ADMET predictions suggested moderate permeability and acceptable drug-likeness but limited intestinal absorption and potential CYP inhibition liabilities. Among candidates, G4L3505 and G4L3506 showed the most favourable overall profiles. These findings support G4 ligands as promising scaffolds for cross-variant SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibition and highlight the value of integrating genomic surveillance with molecular modeling. Experimental assays are required to confirm their inhibitory activity and refine pharmacokinetic properties.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The ongoing SARS-CoV-2 pandemic highlights the need for antivirals effective across emerging variants. This study aimed to explore G-quadruplex (G4) ligands as variant-specific inhibitors targeting the conserved main protease (Mpro).
analysis.study_design_and_population: This in silico study analyzed 5.8 million GISAID sequences to identify mutations in the Mpro enzyme. It focused on SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Omicron (JN.1), and selected representative Mpro structures for screening.
analysis.methods: The study used molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/GBSA calculations to evaluate ligand interactions with the Mpro enzyme. ADMET predictions were also conducted to assess drug-like properties and potential liabilities.
analysis.main_results: Analysis of GISAID sequences revealed frequent mutations K90R (Alpha), G15S (Lambda), and P132H (Omicron, JN.1). Four ligands, G4L3501, G4L3503, G4L3505, and G4L3506, were identified as stably occupying the catalytic pocket through conserved interactions with His41, Cys145, Glu166, and Gln189.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Per-residue energy decomposition confirmed strong stabilization by active-site residues, consistent with the nirmatrelvir (PF-07321332) binding mode. This suggests that G4 ligands could serve as promising scaffolds for cross-variant Mpro inhibition.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the development of G4 ligands as potential antivirals for SARS-CoV-2 and highlight the value of integrating genomic surveillance with molecular modeling to guide drug discovery.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in silico analysis, and experimental assays are required to confirm inhibitory activity and refine pharmacokinetic properties. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on computational methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated G-quadruplex (G4) ligands as potential antivirals targeting the conserved main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 across emerging variants. By analyzing 5.8 million GISAID sequences, the researchers identified mutations guiding the selection of representative Mpro structures for in silico screening. Molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and MM/GBSA calculations revealed four ligands that stably interact with the catalytic pocket through conserved residues. ADMET predictions indicated moderate drug-likeness but potential issues with intestinal absorption and CYP inhibition. The results suggest that G4 ligands could be promising scaffolds for cross-variant Mpro inhibition, though experimental validation is needed. papers.title_zh: 针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2保守主蛋白酶的变体特异性G-四链体配体的计算机模拟研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract The ongoing SARS-CoV-2 pandemic highlights the need for antivirals effective across emerging variants. Targeting the conserved main protease (Mpro), a key enzyme in viral replication, this study explored G-quadruplex (G4) ligands as variant-specific inhibitors. Analysis of 5.8 million GISAID sequences revealed frequent but catalytically distal mutations K90R (Alpha), G15S (Lambda), and P132H (Omicron, JN.1) guiding the selection of representative Mpro structures for in silico screening. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/GBSA calculations identified four ligands G4L3501 (–36.63 kcal/mol), G4L3503 (–40.39 kcal/mol), G4L3505 (–40.54 kcal/mol), and G4L3506 (–20.32 kcal/mol) that stably occupied the catalytic pocket through conserved interactions with His41, Cys145, Glu166, and Gln189. Per-residue energy decomposition confirmed strong stabilization by active-site residues, consistent with the nirmatrelvir (PF-07321332) binding mode. ADMET predictions suggested moderate permeability and acceptable drug-likeness but limited intestinal absorption and potential CYP inhibition liabilities. Among candidates, G4L3505 and G4L3506 showed the most favourable overall profiles. These findings support G4 ligands as promising scaffolds for cross-variant SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibition and highlight the value of integrating genomic surveillance with molecular modeling. Experimental assays are required to confirm their inhibitory activity and refine pharmacokinetic properties.

papers.abstract: Non-human primates (NHPs) retain particular value in emerging viral infection research when questions require integrated analysis of systemic viral kinetics, protective immunity, tissue pathology, or longitudinal outcomes. However, their cost, limited availability, specialized husbandry, and ethical constraints preclude their routine use as default screening platforms. Using severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) as a case study, we compare how rhesus macaques, cynomolgus macaques, African green monkeys, baboons, and marmosets have contributed to studies of pathogenesis, vaccine protection, therapeutic efficacy, immune memory, and post-acute outcomes. We emphasize that these species-question relationships cannot be transferred uncritically to future pathogens; model suitability must be re-established according to receptor usage, tissue tropism, disease phenotype, and experimental objective. AI-guided prediction, human organoids, and organ-on-chip systems can support this process by prioritizing variants and candidates, identifying tissue-specific mechanisms, and refining endpoints before NHP studies begin. We therefore propose a question-driven workflow in which computational and human-relevant platforms narrow the evidence gap before fit-for-purpose NHP validation. This strategy can improve interpretability, reproducibility, and alignment with the 3Rs while preserving NHP use for questions that require intact organism-level biology.

papers.title: COVID-19, immunity, and vaccination: unravelling the interplay of sex, gender, age, and the exposome
papers.abstract: Sex- and gender-related differences profoundly influence immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination but remain insufficiently considered in research and public health strategies. This review explores how sex, gender, age, and the exposome interact to shape susceptibility to coronavirus-19 disease (COVID-19), disease severity, Long COVID, and vaccine-induced immunity. Males experience higher rates of severe disease, hospitalisation, and mortality, whereas females generally mount stronger innate and adaptive immune responses, contributing to greater resilience. These differences arise from a complex interplay between biological factors and gender-related determinants, including occupational exposures, healthcare access, health-related behaviours, socioeconomic conditions, and the microbiota, which contribute to the individual exposome. This review also highlights the impact of ageing on SARS-CoV-2 immunity, highlighting the preserved immune regulation observed in centenarians, which may contribute to protection against severe COVID-19 despite advanced age. Current evidence on Long COVID is discussed, including its higher prevalence among females and the sex-specific immunological pathways that may underlie persistent symptoms. We examine age-, sex-, and gender-related differences in vaccine response, distinguishing efficacy from effectiveness. Although females generally mount stronger antibody responses, this advantage does not necessarily translate into greater clinical protection. The relative benefit of vaccination appears greater in males because of their higher baseline risk of severe disease. Finally, we discuss how exposomic factors, including lifestyle, microbiota composition, and environmental and social determinants, influence vaccine responsiveness and hesitancy. Integrating sex, gender, age, and the exposome perspectives is essential for developing more equitable and personalised strategies to prevent and manage COVID-19 and future emerging diseases.

papers.title: Serious cardiac events in the COVID-19 era in the paediatric population: what did we learn?
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Serious cardiac events, which are frequently associated with myocarditis or arrhythmias, pose serious public health concerns. COVID-19 can increase cardiovascular risks by causing cardiac damage, arrhythmias, and multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children. However, important knowledge gaps about the long-term cardiac effects of COVID-19 still exist. These lead to the possibility of unusual or delayed cardiac consequences and the requirement for specialised monitoring techniques to reduce potential risks, particularly in high-risk populations. This narrative review compares serious cardiac event incidence, mechanisms, and outcomes in adults and children. METHODS: Data were gathered from peer-reviewed studies between 2019 and 2025, such as systematic reviews, clinical reports, and cohort analyses. Focus was placed on the potential contribution of COVID-19-related cardiac events. Key research and clinical practice gaps were identified by analysing paediatric and adult populations in terms of diagnostic methods, management techniques, and long-term results. RESULTS: While vaccine-related cardiac complications are still uncommon, COVID-19 infection is linked to an increased risk of serious cardiac events in adults. Paediatric serious cardiac events, on the other hand, are rare but frequently associated with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children, and there have been rare, documented vaccine-associated deaths in this population. CONCLUSION: Significant findings reveal clear patterns in serious cardiac events mechanisms, with age-dependent differences in the severity and prognosis of COVID-19-related myocarditis, arrhythmias, and long QT syndrome, among others. These variations highlight the necessity of age-appropriate risk assessment and management techniques. It highlights the increased risk of such events in adults linked to COVID-19 infection, while noting that pediatric cases are rare but often tied to multisystem inflammatory syndrome. papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 severity and vaccination, pneumonia, and the risk of Stroke: A nationwide, nested case-control study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background : Infections, including SARS-CoV-2, may increase stroke risk, but the roles of COVID-19 severity, vaccination, and comparison with other respiratory infections remain unclear. This study examined the association between COVID-19, its severity, and vaccination status with the incidence of new-onset total stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and ischemic stroke in a nationwide sample of adults aged ≥50 years. Methods: A nested case-control study was conducted within the largest healthcare provider in Israel. Stroke-free individuals were followed-up from March 2020 to May 2022. Incident total, ICH and ischemic stroke cases were matched 1:10 to controls by age, sex, and index date. Laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, COVID-19 severity, vaccination status, and pneumonia were ascertained from electronic health records, and multivariable conditional logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for stroke. Results: Among 1,198,088 eligible participants, 11,974 individuals with incident total stroke were matched to 119,740 controls. COVID-19 was associated with an increased stroke risk (OR=1.23; 95% CI 1.16-1.30; P Conclusions: COVID-19 requiring hospitalization confers an acute, time-limited increase in stroke risk, of a magnitude somewhat lower than that observed after pneumonia. These findings support targeted cerebrovascular surveillance following hospitalization for respiratory infection. Vaccination was associated with lower stroke risk, although this observational association warrants cautious interpretation.

Methods: A nested case-control study was conducted within the largest healthcare provider in Israel. Stroke-free individuals were followed-up from March 2020 to May 2022. Incident total, ICH and ischemic stroke cases were matched 1:10 to controls by age, sex, and index date. Laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, COVID-19 severity, vaccination status, and pneumonia were ascertained from electronic health records, and multivariable conditional logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for stroke. Results: Among 1,198,088 eligible participants, 11,974 individuals with incident total stroke were matched to 119,740 controls. COVID-19 was associated with an increased stroke risk (OR=1.23; 95% CI 1.16-1.30; P Conclusions: COVID-19 requiring hospitalization confers an acute, time-limited increase in stroke risk, of a magnitude somewhat lower than that observed after pneumonia. These findings support targeted cerebrovascular surveillance following hospitalization for respiratory infection. Vaccination was associated with lower stroke risk, although this observational association warrants cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection, its severity, and vaccination status with the risk of stroke in adults aged ≥50 years. Conducted as a nationwide nested case-control study within Israel's largest healthcare provider, the research followed stroke-free individuals from March 2020 to May 2022. It found that COVID-19 was linked to an increased stroke risk (OR=1.23; 95% CI 1.16-1.30; P < 0.001), while vaccination was associated with lower risk. The authors suggest that cerebrovascular surveillance should be targeted following hospitalization for respiratory infections. However, the observational nature of the study means the link between vaccination and reduced stroke risk requires careful interpretation. The study provides insights into the acute stroke risk associated with SARS-CoV-2 hospitalization, though it does not establish causality.

papers.title: Emerging Biomarkers Across the Clinical Spectrum of SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Long COVID
papers.abstract: Long COVID, also referred to in the literature as postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) or postacute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS), is a chronic and heterogeneous multisystem condition persisting beyond acute COVID-19. For consistency, this review uses the term “Long COVID” throughout; PASC and PACS are noted only where they reflect the terminology used by a specific cited study. The absence of validated, clinically actionable biomarkers remains a major barrier to diagnosis, risk stratification, and targeted intervention. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on candidate biomarkers relevant to SARS-CoV-2 infection, with particular attention to their mechanistic, clinical and translational relevance to long COVID specifically. Reflecting the fact that many candidate markers have been characterised primarily in acute or severe COVID-19, we explicitly indicate, for each biomarker domain, the strength and directness of the evidence linking it to long COVID as opposed to acute disease severity alone, and we distinguish exploratory candidates from those with more established clinical utility. Biomarkers are organised by domain virological, immunological/inflammatory, hematological/vascular, cardiovascular, metabolic/neuroendocrine, neurocognitive, and genetic/epigenetic beginning with virological and host-response markers, which we consider the most biologically direct evidence of ongoing SARS-CoV-2-related pathology, and closing with an integrative discussion of multiomics approaches. We also address biomarker overlap with other postinfectious and chronic inflammatory conditions, notably myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), and the specific contribution of host genetic variation, including HLA haplotypes, to long COVID susceptibility. Relative to prior systematic reviews of long COVID biomarkers, this review’s distinguishing contribution is its explicit separation of acute-phase from chronic-phase evidence, its integration of genetic, epigenetic, and multiomics data within a single mechanistic framework, and its tiered classification of biomarkers by clinical readiness. Clinically, biomarker signatures are linked to core symptom clusters spanning respiratory, cardiovascular, neurological, metabolic and neuropsychiatric domains, underlining the potential for biomarker-informed patient classification, monitoring and targeted therapy, while emphasizing that most candidates currently remain exploratory and require validation in large, prospective, multicenter cohorts before clinical adoption.

papers.title: Immunogenicity and vaccine effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines in people on immunosuppressive therapies
papers.abstract: Abstract Neutralizing antibodies are a correlate of protection (CoP) of SARS-CoV-2 vaccine efficacy. However, data informing CoPs often explicitly exclude people on immunosuppressive therapies who are at an increased risk of symptomatic and severe COVID-19, delayed viral clearance, and death. Investigating the relationship between antibodies and protection for people on immunosuppressive therapies could provide insights into mechanisms of protection. We performed a systematic search to identify studies reporting SARS-CoV-2 binding antibody levels after mRNA vaccination in people with hematological malignancies, neurological disorders, rheumatic diseases, and mixed immune-mediated inflammatory disorders (IMIDs) on immunosuppressive therapies including B-cell depletion, JAK inhibitors, and S1P inhibitors, as well as healthy controls. Binding antibody levels varied between cohorts receiving different immunosuppressive treatments. Compared to healthy controls the lowest antibody levels were observed in subjects treated with B-cell depletion (54.5-fold reduction, 95% CI: 34.5-86.2) and S1P inhibitors (24.8-fold reduction, 95% CI: 13.2-46.7). To assess the association between antibody level and protection, we used data from a previous study of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness in people with the same underlying conditions. We linked vaccine effectiveness estimates with the predicted antibody level in people on immunosuppressive therapies (using antibody data including this meta-analysis of binding antibody levels). Predicted neutralizing antibody levels were correlated with vaccine effectiveness both for infection and hospitalization (p<0.0001 and p<0.0001, respectively). However, we found that for any given antibody level, people who are immunosuppressed had lower protection against infection and hospitalization than a healthy population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between neutralizing antibodies and protection against SARS-CoV-2 in people on immunosuppressive therapies, as data on correlates of protection often exclude these individuals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A systematic search was conducted to identify studies on SARS-CoV-2 binding antibody levels after mRNA vaccination in people with hematological malignancies, neurological disorders, rheumatic diseases, and mixed immune-mediated inflammatory disorders on immunosuppressive therapies, as well as healthy controls.
analysis.methods: The study used data from a previous analysis of vaccine effectiveness in people with the same underlying conditions and linked these estimates with predicted antibody levels derived from a meta-analysis of binding antibody levels.
analysis.main_results: Binding antibody levels varied across cohorts receiving different immunosuppressive treatments, with the lowest levels observed in those treated with B-cell depletion and S1P inhibitors. Predicted neutralizing antibody levels were correlated with vaccine effectiveness for both infection and hospitalization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that antibody levels are associated with vaccine effectiveness, but emphasized that immunosuppressed individuals have lower protection at any given antibody level compared to healthy populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform strategies for monitoring vaccine responses in immunosuppressed individuals and guide the development of more effective vaccination protocols for this vulnerable group.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on data from a previous analysis and predicted antibody levels, which may introduce limitations in the accuracy of the correlation between antibody levels and protection, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between neutralizing antibodies and protection against SARS-CoV-2 in people on immunosuppressive therapies, as existing data often excludes these individuals. A systematic search identified antibody levels after mRNA vaccination in various immune conditions, revealing significant reductions in B-cell depletion and S1P inhibitor treatments. The authors linked these antibody levels with vaccine effectiveness data from a prior study, finding a correlation between antibody levels and protection against infection and hospitalization. However, they noted that immunosuppressed individuals have lower protection at any given antibody level compared to healthy controls. These results may inform strategies for monitoring vaccine responses in immunosuppressed populations. The study's reliance on predicted antibody levels and prior data limits its evidence strength, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

papers.title: Immune dysfunction in chronic lymphocytic leukemia : translational and epidemiological studies during the COVID-19 pandemic
papers.abstract: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is a chronic malignancy of mature B lymphocytes with increasing prevalence in Sweden. CLL is associated with substantial immune deficiency, making patients more susceptible to infections and less responsive to conventional vaccines. CLL therapy may further aggravate immunosuppression. The COVID-19 pandemic therefore raised important questions about the impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination in individuals with CLL. This thesis addresses some of these questions. Study I investigated the clinical and immunological outcome of SARS-CoV-2 infection in CLL patients at the beginning of the pandemic. We included all known and PCR-verified COVID-19 cases among CLL patients in the Stockholm region between 1 March 2020 and 31 March 2021. Clinical data were collected from medical records, and patients who recovered were followed with repeated blood and saliva samples for up to 12 months to assess B and T cell responses. Among 60 patients, 77% required hospitalization, 24% intensive care, and approximately 30% died. Among convalescents (n=40), 82% seroconverted, 68% had detectable SARS-CoV-2-specific antibodies in saliva, and T cell immune responses was detected in 14/17 (82%). Serum antibodies remained detectable in approximately 75% at 6 and 12 months. Clinical outcomes improved during the second half of the study period. Study II evaluated B and T cell responses after two doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA vaccine BNT162b2 in 52 CLL patients and 41 healthy controls participating in the COVAXID prospective trial. The CLL cohort included patients with untreated indolent CLL (n=14), previous immunochemotherapy including rituximab >12 months earlier (n=14), ongoing BTKi treatment (n=14), or discontinued BTKi treatment due to remission (n=10). Sixty percent of CLL patients seroconverted, with low antibody titers (median 25 U/ml), compared to 100% of controls (median 2600 U/ml). T cell responses occurred in 29% of CLL patients versus 60% of controls. Responses were more frequent after discontinuation of BTKi, whereas patients currently receiving BTKi treatment had the lowest seroconversion and T cell response rates. Fifteen patients (29%) were double-negative, and 11/15 had ongoing BTKi treatment. Study III investigated hybrid immunity in the cohort from Study I, i.e. patients who had recovered from COVID-19 and subsequently received SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. Blood and saliva samples were collected before vaccination, after the second vaccine dose, and before and after the third dose. Serum antibody titers increased significantly after two doses, from a median of 47 U/ml to 12,500 U/ml. Titers decreased by approximately 50% between the second and third dose (median interval 5 months), to then increase even further after the third dose. SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell reactivity and salivary antibodies also increased after vaccination, but mainly after the third dose. Study IV examined SARS-CoV-2 vaccine uptake among individuals with CLL in Sweden using six national health and sociodemographic registries. We included 6,304 individuals aged 18-90 years diagnosed with CLL up to November 30, 2022, and followed vaccination uptake from December 27, 2020 (date of first SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in Sweden), to February 28, 2023. Overall uptake was higher than age-standardized nationwide uptake: 94% received two doses, 88% three doses, 78% four doses, and 56% five doses. However, 253 individuals remained unvaccinated, and substantial disparities were observed by age, region of birth, and income. These disparities were greatest for the fourth and fifth doses; among individuals born abroad and in the lowest income quartile, uptake was only 49% and 24%, respectively, for the fourth and fifth doses. Study V analyzed COVID-19-related mortality and hospitalization over the first three years of the pandemic in Sweden. Cross-linked data from ten national registries were used to compare individuals with CLL with the general population, stratified by age, time period/SARS-CoV-2 variant, and vaccination status. Among 8,275,839 individuals born 1930-2003, including 6,653 with CLL, 2,088,163 first SARS-CoV-2 infections were identified between February 1, 2020, and February 27, 2023, including 1,289 in individuals with CLL. The adjusted risk ratio (aRR) for 90-day all-cause mortality was 1.70 in CLL versus comparators and 4.17 among those younger than 65 years; the overall mortality rate in this age group was 3.6%. Overall mortality was highest during the Wild-type period but remained 12% during the Omicron era, with an aRR of 1.49. CLL patients receiving Bcl-2i, BTKi, PI3Ki, or corticosteroids at time of infection showed increased risk of hospitalization and death compared to CLL patients not treated with these drugs. However, aRRs for poor outcomes decreased with each vaccine dose vs comparators with the corresponding vaccination status, suggesting protection against severe COVID-19 also in individuals with CLL. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination on individuals with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) during the COVID-19 pandemic, given the known immune deficiencies in CLL patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study included five distinct investigations. analysis.main_results: In Study I, 77% of CLL patients required hospitalization, 24% needed intensive care, and approximately 30% died. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on registry data and medical records, which may introduce bias or missing information. However, the evidence is robust due to the use of multiple national datasets and longitudinal tracking of vaccine uptake.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination on individuals with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) during the COVID-19 pandemic. It includes five investigations: Study I assessed clinical and immunological outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection in CLL patients, revealing high hospitalization and mortality rates. Study II evaluated vaccine responses in CLL patients and healthy controls, showing lower seroconversion and T cell responses in CLL patients. Study IV analyzed vaccine uptake in Sweden, finding higher rates among CLL patients than the general population but significant disparities by age, region of birth, and income. Study V compared mortality and hospitalization rates between CLL patients and the general population, noting increased risks for younger patients and those on certain treatments. The findings suggest that while CLL patients face heightened risks from SARS-CoV-2, vaccination reduces these risks. The study highlights the importance of targeted vaccination strategies and addressing disparities in vaccine access for this vulnerable group.
